agent-architecture.label: Agent architecture
agent-architecture.definition: Combine a model, tools, memory, control flow, and an environment into an agent.

workflow-agent.label: Workflows versus agents
workflow-agent.definition: Distinguish fixed program control flow from model-directed control flow.

reasoning.label: Multi-step reasoning
reasoning.definition: Use intermediate reasoning steps to solve a task.

cot.label: Chain of thought
cot.definition: Generate intermediate reasoning steps before a final answer.

self-consistency.label: Self-consistency
self-consistency.definition: Sample several reasoning paths and combine their answers.

reflection.label: Reflection and self-correction
reflection.definition: Use feedback about an attempt to revise reasoning or future actions.

reflexion.label: Reflexion
reflexion.definition: Store verbal feedback from earlier attempts to improve later attempts.

planning.label: Planning and task decomposition
planning.definition: Choose and organize steps or subtasks before or during action.

react.label: ReAct
react.definition: Alternate reasoning, tool actions, and observations.

codeact.label: CodeAct
codeact.definition: Use executable code as the agent action interface.

plan-execute.label: Plan then execute
plan-execute.definition: Separate a planning stage from the execution of the planned steps.

prompt-chain.label: Prompt chaining
prompt-chain.definition: Pass the output of one model step into the next step.

routing.label: Routing
routing.definition: Choose a specialized path or component for an input.

parallelization.label: Parallel execution
parallelization.definition: Run independent tasks at the same time and combine results.

orchestrator-workers.label: Orchestrator and workers
orchestrator-workers.definition: Let a coordinator split work and assign subtasks to worker agents.

critic-loop.label: Evaluator and optimizer loop
critic-loop.definition: Use a separate evaluator to guide repeated improvement of an output.

llm-foundations.label: Language model foundations
llm-foundations.definition: Explain next-token modeling and the main parts of a language model.

transformer.label: Transformer and attention
transformer.definition: Use attention-based neural networks to model token sequences.

decoding.label: Decoding and sampling
decoding.definition: Choose output tokens from model probabilities.

structured-output.label: Structured output and constrained decoding
structured-output.definition: Constrain model output to a schema or a set of valid tokens.

inference-scaling.label: Inference-time scaling
inference-scaling.definition: Spend more inference compute on reasoning, search, or repeated attempts.

prompting.label: Prompt design
prompting.definition: Design instructions, examples, and role messages to guide a model.

few-shot.label: Few-shot prompting
few-shot.definition: Include examples in a prompt to guide the response.

prompt-optimization.label: Automatic prompt optimization
prompt-optimization.definition: Use measured feedback to search for better instructions or examples.

sft.label: Supervised fine-tuning
sft.definition: Train a model on examples of desired responses or action trajectories.

model-training.label: Model training and post-training
model-training.definition: Train model weights before or after initial pretraining.

rl.label: Reinforcement learning
rl.definition: Learn a policy by using rewards from interaction.

ppo.label: Proximal policy optimization
ppo.definition: Update a policy with a clipped objective to limit policy changes.

grpo.label: Group relative policy optimization
grpo.definition: Compare rewards within groups of sampled outputs to update a policy.

distillation.label: Knowledge distillation
distillation.definition: Train a model to follow the outputs or behavior of a teacher model.

rag.label: Retrieval-augmented generation
rag.definition: Retrieve external information and use it to generate an answer.

chunking.label: Document chunking and indexing
chunking.definition: Split source documents and build an index for retrieval.

embeddings.label: Embedding-based retrieval
embeddings.definition: Encode queries and documents as vectors and retrieve similar documents.

sparse-retrieval.label: Sparse retrieval
sparse-retrieval.definition: Rank documents with token-based relevance scores.

hybrid-search.label: Hybrid retrieval
hybrid-search.definition: Combine lexical and embedding-based retrieval results.

reranking.label: Reranking and late interaction
reranking.definition: Rescore retrieved candidates with richer query-document comparisons.

graph-rag.label: Graph-based retrieval
graph-rag.definition: Use graph relations or graph summaries to support retrieval.

agentic-rag.label: Agentic retrieval
agentic-rag.definition: Let an agent decide when and how to retrieve and revise a search.

retrieval-eval.label: Retrieval evaluation
retrieval-eval.definition: Measure whether retrieval returns relevant evidence.

tool-use.label: Tool use and function calling
tool-use.definition: Let a model choose and call external functions and consume their results.

tool-discovery.label: Tool discovery and selection
tool-discovery.definition: Find and select relevant tools from available tool descriptions.

mcp.label: Model Context Protocol
mcp.definition: Connect agent hosts and tool servers through a shared tool interface.

tool-eval.label: Tool-call evaluation
tool-eval.definition: Check selected tools, arguments, execution, and tool-use outcomes.

frameworks.label: Agent frameworks and orchestration
frameworks.definition: Use reusable components and control flow to build agent systems.

dspy.label: DSPy
dspy.definition: Build and optimize language model programs with signatures, modules, and optimizers.

langgraph.label: LangGraph
langgraph.definition: Build stateful model workflows with nodes, edges, and graph state.

harness.label: Agent harness design
harness.definition: Design the runtime around a model, including tools, state, limits, and execution.

durable-execution.label: Durable execution and recovery
durable-execution.definition: Persist execution state and recover work after failures or pauses.

observability.label: Tracing and observability
observability.definition: Record agent steps and inspect behavior, failures, and runtime measurements.

context-engineering.label: Context engineering
context-engineering.definition: Select and organize the information supplied to a model for each step.

compaction.label: Context summarization and compaction
compaction.definition: Replace long interaction history with a shorter useful representation.

context-offload.label: Context offloading
context-offload.definition: Store information outside the active prompt and load it when needed.

observation-masking.label: Observation masking
observation-masking.definition: Remove or hide older tool outputs while keeping useful interaction structure.

context-isolation.label: Context isolation
context-isolation.definition: Give a task or subagent a separate context to limit interference.

progressive-disclosure.label: Progressive disclosure
progressive-disclosure.definition: Load instructions or tool details only when the current task needs them.

memory.label: Agent memory
memory.definition: Store and reuse information across steps or interactions.

working-memory.label: Working memory
working-memory.definition: Keep information needed for the current task in active context.

episodic-memory.label: Episodic memory
episodic-memory.definition: Store events or past experiences that an agent can recall.

semantic-memory.label: Semantic memory
semantic-memory.definition: Store facts and general knowledge for later use.

procedural-memory.label: Procedural memory and skills
procedural-memory.definition: Store reusable procedures or skills that guide actions.

tiered-memory.label: Tiered memory
tiered-memory.definition: Move information between memory levels with different capacity and access costs.

memory-maintenance.label: Memory maintenance and consolidation
memory-maintenance.definition: Update, combine, remove, or reorganize stored memories.

memory-eval.label: Memory evaluation
memory-eval.definition: Measure recall, updating, temporal reasoning, and useful memory use.

multi-agent.label: Multi-agent systems
multi-agent.definition: Use several agents that interact to solve tasks.

agent-handoff.label: Agent handoffs
agent-handoff.definition: Transfer control and relevant information from one agent to another.

agent-as-tool.label: Agent as a tool
agent-as-tool.definition: Call a specialist agent as a tool while the caller keeps control.

shared-memory.label: Shared memory and task coordination
shared-memory.definition: Coordinate agents through shared state, task records, or message stores.

a2a.label: Agent2Agent protocol
a2a.definition: Describe and exchange tasks between agents through a shared protocol.

worktree-isolation.label: Workspace isolation
worktree-isolation.definition: Give agents separate working directories to prevent conflicting file changes.

multi-agent-failures.label: Multi-agent failure analysis
multi-agent-failures.definition: Analyze coordination failures, conflicting goals, and harmful group behavior.

data-curation.label: Training data selection and quality
data-curation.definition: Select and check useful tasks, demonstrations, and trajectories.

synthetic-data.label: Synthetic data and trajectory generation
synthetic-data.definition: Generate tasks, examples, or agent rollouts for training or testing.

human-demos.label: Human demonstrations and feedback
human-demos.definition: Collect human actions or feedback to train or improve an agent.

evaluation.label: Agent evaluation and benchmarks
evaluation.definition: Measure agent behavior and outcomes with defined tasks and scores.

benchmark-design.label: Benchmark and test-set design
benchmark-design.definition: Define tasks, environments, stopping rules, and scoring for evaluation.

code-grader.label: Code-based evaluators
code-grader.definition: Use deterministic code or tests to score agent behavior or outputs.

human-eval.label: Human evaluation
human-eval.definition: Use human judgments or labels to assess agent behavior or outputs.

llm-judge.label: LLM as a judge
llm-judge.definition: Use a language model to score another system with stated criteria.

judge-validation.label: Judge validation and bias
judge-validation.definition: Check evaluator agreement, accuracy, and bias against trusted labels.

rubrics.label: Evaluation rubrics
rubrics.definition: Define explicit criteria and rating rules for judgments.

reliability.label: Reliability and repeated-run evaluation
reliability.definition: Measure variation and success across repeated agent runs.

reward-hacking.label: Reward hacking and evaluation gaming
reward-hacking.definition: Exploit a reward or scoring rule without meeting the intended task.

coding-agents.label: Coding and terminal agents
coding-agents.definition: Use agents to write, edit, test, or run code and command-line tasks.

safety.label: Agent safety and guardrails
safety.definition: Limit harmful agent actions and enforce task or use constraints.

prompt-injection.label: Prompt injection
prompt-injection.definition: Untrusted content attempts to redirect an agent or override instructions.

privacy.label: Privacy and user data protection
privacy.definition: Control disclosure and use of private user information.

sandboxing.label: Sandboxed execution
sandboxing.definition: Run code or tools inside a restricted environment.

hitl.label: Human oversight and approval
hitl.definition: Pause or route an agent decision to a person for review or approval.

personalization.label: Personalization and user modeling
personalization.definition: Adapt agent behavior to a user's preferences, history, or needs.

proactive.label: Proactive and mixed-initiative agents
proactive.definition: Let an agent decide when to initiate useful actions or interaction.
